name: השלמה לריבוע ופתרון משוואה ריבועית עם שורשים שלמים (באנגלית)
questiontext:
Give the following quadratic in completed square form i.e. in the form \(\left( x+a \right)^2+b.\)

\[ {{CT:0}} \]

a
[[input:ans1]]
[[validation:ans1]]
[[feedback:prt2]]
b

Solve the quadratic equation \({{CT:0}}=0\). Give your answer as a set \(\left(\mbox e.g.\ \left\{x_1 , x_2\right\} \right)\):

[[input:ans2]]
[[validation:ans2]]
[[feedback:prt1]]
generalfeedback:
Outline: Completing the square writes the quadratic as a square plus a constant, so the first-degree term disappears. Then the equation is solved by isolating the square and taking the square root with both signs.
Step 1 — Completing the square (part a)
The coefficient of \({{CT:1}}\) is \({{CT:2}}\); half of it is \({{CT:3}}\). Squaring the bracket with this number:

\[ {{CT:4}}={{CT:5}} \]

so the first two terms of the quadratic are this square minus \({{CT:6}}\):

\[ {{CT:7}}={{CT:4}}-{{CT:6}} \]

Hence[[if test="{{CT:18}}"]]

\[ {{CT:0}}={{CT:4}}-{{CT:6}} \]

[[else]]

\[ {{CT:0}}=\left({{CT:4}}-{{CT:6}}\right)[[if test="{{CT:19}}"]]+{{CT:8}}[[else]]-{{CT:9}}[[/if]] \]

[[/if]]and the completed square form is

\[ {{CT:0}}={{CT:10}} \]

Step 2 — Solving the equation (part b)
Using part a, the equation \({{CT:0}}=0\) becomes

\[ {{CT:10}}=0 \]

Moving the constant to the right-hand side:

\[ {{CT:4}}={{CT:11}} \]

Taking the square root (remember both signs), since \({{CT:11}}={{CT:12}}^2\):

\[ {{CT:13}}=\pm {{CT:12}} \]

Subtracting \({{CT:3}}\) from both sides:

\[ {{CT:1}}={{CT:14}}\pm {{CT:12}} \]

so \({{CT:1}}={{CT:15}}\) or \({{CT:1}}={{CT:16}}\). The solution set is

\[ {{CT:1}}\in {{CT:17}} \]

on_false.feedback: Part b — incorrect. Use part a: isolate the square, take the square root with both signs, and solve.
Part a — incorrect. The number in the bracket is half the coefficient of the first-degree term; then adjust the constant so that the expression stays equal to the original quadratic.
